title: Monkeypox Virus Surveillance in Wastewater, North Carolina, USA, October 2023-May 2025.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study was needed to assess possible unrecognized transmission of mpox virus in North Carolina, USA, following a new case identified in September 2023 after a 5-month gap since the last report. The objective was to evaluate the utility of wastewater surveillance for detecting mpox virus activity.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A wastewater surveillance study was conducted from October 29, 2023, to May 2025, across 16 treatment plants serving approximately 2 million residents. The study included 801 samples collected during this period.
analysis.methods: Wastewater samples were analyzed for mpox virus detections using a +17-day window aligned with clinical cases. The study also included testing for nonvariola orthopoxvirus at select wastewater sites.
analysis.main_results: Overall sensitivity of identifying the presence of >1 temporally aligned mpox case within a sewershed was 10.6% (95% CI 6.5%-16.7%); specificity was 95.1% (95% CI 93.2%-96.5%), positive predictive value was 31.9% (95% CI 20.4%-46.2%), and negative predictive value was 83.2% (95% CI 80.3%-85.7%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that wastewater surveillance showed low sensitivity but provided complementary awareness for public health response. They noted that restricting detections above the limit of detection reduced sensitivity but increased specificity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that wastewater surveillance can offer additional insights for public health monitoring of mpox virus, even with limited sensitivity, and may support early detection and response strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study had low sensitivity in detecting mpox virus, which may limit its effectiveness for surveillance. The evidence strength is moderate due to the limited sensitivity and the potential for false negatives.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the utility of wastewater surveillance for detecting mpox virus activity in North Carolina, USA, from October 2023 to May 2025. Following a new mpox case identified in September 2023, the researchers collected 801 samples across 16 treatment plants to assess possible unrecognized transmission. They analyzed wastewater detections and clinical cases using a 17-day window and reported that the overall sensitivity of identifying temporally aligned mpox cases was 10.6%, while specificity was 95.1%. The study found that restricting detections above the limit of detection increased specificity but reduced sensitivity. The authors interpreted that wastewater surveillance provided complementary awareness for public health response despite its low sensitivity. They noted that the findings may support early detection strategies but highlighted the limitations of the method in terms of sensitivity and potential for false negatives. The evidence strength is moderate due to these limitations.

title: Tell people and lose what I have: Care-seeking, concealment, and disclosure during Sierra Leone’s 2025 clade IIb mpox outbreak

analysis.research_question_and_background: During Sierra Leone's 2025 clade IIb mpox outbreak, care-seeking occurred in a social context where formal presentation could expose symptoms, sexualised assumptions, and private relationships to families, workplaces, neighbours, and surveillance systems. The study aimed to understand the social and health system factors influencing care-seeking behaviors during the outbreak.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A focused thematic analysis was conducted across Western Area Urban, Western Area Rural, Bo, and Kenema from 10 March to 28 August 2025, involving 70 transcripts from 42 survivor interviews and 28 contextual transcripts from healthcare workers, contact tracers, and community members.
analysis.methods: The analysis used the Framework Method, including dual coding, reflexive memos, matrix charting, and member checking with survivor participants.
analysis.main_results: Four linked processes were identified: protective misrecognition through socially safer diagnostic categories; disclosure risk as the point where stigma, cost, distance, relationship risk, and service trust converged; health system co-production of delay through early diagnostic uncertainty, referral gaps, and limited diagnostic access; and enabling conditions that made care-seeking safer, especially trusted intermediaries and visible confidentiality practices.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study provided a nuanced understanding of how disclosure decisions were influenced by social and health system factors, highlighting the importance of confidentiality, intermediaries, and contact-tracing systems in outbreak preparedness.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the design of confidentiality, intermediary, and contact-tracing systems that make disclosure safe enough to perform, thereby improving care-seeking behaviors during mpox outbreaks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's design limitations include the potential for selection bias and the reliance on self-reported data. The evidence strength is moderate due to the qualitative nature of the data and the need for further quantitative validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study explored care-seeking behaviors during Sierra Leone's 2025 clade IIb mpox outbreak, revealing how social and health system factors influenced disclosure decisions. The findings suggest the need for improved confidentiality and intermediary systems to enhance care-seeking during mpox outbreaks.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to detect monkeypox virus (MPXV) in skin lesions of individuals in Nigeria, addressing the need for early detection and management of mpox cases to prevent further spread.

analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings underscore the benefit of One Health in passive surveillance at health and allied facilities, highlighting the importance of early detection and referral for management.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study's findings can inform surveillance and management strategies for mpox, emphasizing the role of One Health in early detection and prevention.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's sample size was limited to 110 individuals, and the findings are specific to the study setting, limiting generalizability.

In this study, we established an intranasal BALB/c mouse model of MPXV clade Ib infection and compared its pathogenicity with that of clade IIb. Compared with clade IIb, clade Ib infection showed faster disease progression, higher pulmonary viral burden at later stages of infection, and more severe lung pathology. Antiviral evaluation showed that tecovirimat and cidofovir were active against both clades, although a higher dose of cidofovir was required to achieve protection in the clade Ib infection model. The global emergence of monkeypox virus (MPXV) clade IIb since 2022, together with the recent spread of clade Ib, underscores the continuing public health threat posed by MPXV. Single-cell transcriptome and cytokine response analyses further uncovered clade-specific differences in pulmonary immune cell landscapes, the distribution of MPXV-positive cells, and the expression patterns of key inflammatory mediators at specific time points.

title: The risk of mpox false positive results in high transmission settings: evidence from a multi-site observational study in DR Congo.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to quantify the impact of environmental monkeypox virus (MPXV) DNA on routine mpox diagnosis and case ascertainment during a widespread outbreak in DR Congo, addressing the challenge of environmental viral DNA contamination in highly sensitive assays.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A multi-site observational study was conducted across four locations in DR Congo, involving 2724 people with mpox-compatible illness who attended mpox treatment centres between May 2024 and April 2026.
analysis.methods: Cycle threshold (Ct) values from qPCR tests were collected, and surface sampling of clinic and laboratory environments was performed in two locations. A Bayesian latent class model was developed to distinguish true MPXV infections from environmentally derived MPXV DNA, and model-based classifications were externally evaluated with serological data.
analysis.main_results: The study estimated that 35% of qPCR results with Ct values less than 40 were false positives due to environmental MPXV DNA. Lowering the diagnostic cutoff to Ct values less than 37 reduced the false positive rate to 18%, and reducing it to less than 34 reduced it to 5%.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: More than one in three qPCR-positive mpox diagnoses might have been driven by environmental MPXV DNA, with serological data supporting this finding. Optimizing Ct value cutoffs and additional investigation could improve diagnostic specificity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that decontamination of clinical areas, optimized Ct value cutoffs, and additional investigation could substantially improve mpox diagnosis specificity while preserving sensitivity.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's multi-site design and use of serological data for external validation support the findings, but the sample size and specific environmental conditions in DR Congo may limit generalizability.

analysis.summary_en: This study quantified the impact of environmental MPXV DNA on mpox diagnosis in DR Congo, estimating that 35% of qPCR results were false positives. Optimizing Ct value cutoffs and additional investigation could improve diagnostic specificity.

title: Global immuno-epidemiology and the persistence of mpox clade IIb in MSM

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand how mpox clade IIb persisted and transitioned to endemic circulation among men who have sex with men (MSM) globally, following a decline in case numbers in 2022 due to behavior change and immunization.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study utilized an agent-based model of mpox transmission on the Berlin MSM sexual contact network, incorporating viral shedding kinetics, vaccination, infection-derived immunity, immune waning, and case importations, with the model calibrated using data from 2022.
analysis.methods: The model incorporated viral shedding kinetics, vaccination, infection-derived immunity, immune waning, and case importations, and was calibrated using data from 2022 to estimate the probability of mpox extinction in Berlin and across a European MSM metapopulation.
analysis.main_results: The model estimated that the probability of mpox extinction in Berlin exceeded 80% in 2023, with the probability reducing to less than 60% when extended to a European MSM metapopulation, and nearly zero when incorporating global metapopulation dynamics.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found that mpox persistence was enabled by epidemic asynchrony, where transmission continued in Asia long enough for immune waning to partially restore transmission potential in Europe, enabling subsequent re-importation and endemic circulation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the role of global immuno-epidemiology in enabling mpox persistence and emphasize the importance of coordinated international surveillance and control efforts.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the reliance on a model for estimating extinction probabilities, which may not fully capture real-world complexities, and the need for further validation through empirical data.

analysis.summary_en: This study used an agent-based model to understand how mpox clade IIb persisted among men who have sex with men globally, finding that persistence was enabled by epidemic asynchrony and emphasizing the need for coordinated international surveillance.

title: Global immuno-epidemiology and the persistence of mpox clade IIb in MSM

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand how mpox clade IIb persisted globally in men who have sex with men (MSM) despite declining case numbers in Europe and Norther America by summer 2022.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed mpox transmission dynamics in the Berlin MSM sexual contact network and extended the analysis to a European MSM metapopulation, incorporating global dynamics to assess persistence.
analysis.methods: An agent-based model was developed to simulate mpox transmission, integrating viral shedding kinetics, vaccination, infection-derived immunity, immune waning, and case importations.
analysis.main_results: The model estimated that the probability of mpox extinction in Berlin exceeded 80% in 2023, but extending the analysis to a global metapopulation reduced this probability to nearly zero.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that mpox persistence was enabled by epidemic asynchrony, where transmission continued in Asia while it declined in Europe/the Americas, allowing for immune waning and subsequent re-importation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the importance of coordinated international surveillance and control efforts to address mpox persistence in connected global MSM networks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on model-based findings and phylogenetic evidence, which may have limitations in capturing real-world complexities, but the evidence is supported by multiple data sources.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how mpox clade IIb persisted globally in men who have sex with men (MSM) despite declining case numbers in Europe and North America by summer 2022. Using an agent-based model of transmission on the Berlin MSM sexual contact network, the authors found that mpox extinction probability in Berlin exceeded 80% in 2023 due to fragmented transmission networks. However, extending the analysis to a European metapopulation reduced this probability to less than 60%, and incorporating global dynamics brought it nearly to zero. The authors suggest that mpox persistence is enabled by epidemic asynchrony, where transmission continues in Asia while it declines in Europe and the Americas, allowing immune waning and subsequent re-importation. These model-based findings are supported by phylogenetic evidence linking active German transmission clusters to re-importation from the Americas or emergence from Asia. The study emphasizes the role of global immuno-epidemiology in mpox persistence and underscores the need for coordinated international surveillance and control efforts. The evidence is considered moderate due to reliance on modeling and phylogenetic data, which may not fully capture real-world complexities.

title: Mpox in Africa: one year continental response outcomes and way forward.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Following the declaration of mpox as both a global and continental public health emergency in August 2024, the Joint Incident Management Support Team (IMST), co-led by the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) and the WHO, was activated in Kinshasa, DRC to coordinate the continental mpox response. This article highlights the first year's epidemiological and operational findings.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Key performance indicators across eight IMST pillars (coordination, surveillance, laboratory, case management, infection prevention and control, risk communication and community engagement (RCCE), vaccination and research) were descriptively analysed using data from 28 African Union Member States from January 2024 to August 2025. Operational achievements included 87% surveillance completeness, 72% contact tracing completeness and improved average laboratory turnaround time from >5 days to 2 days.
analysis.methods: The study used descriptive analysis of key performance indicators across eight IMST pillars using data from 28 African Union Member States from January 2024 to August 2025. Future focus must shift from emergency action to durable, sustained investment in national and sub-national health security architecture using a multisectoral whole of government approach.
analysis.main_results: A total of 49 803 confirmed cases and 240 deaths (CFR 0.5%) were recorded across 28 countries. The response was supported with US$977 million as tracked by the IMST. Laboratory testing capacity expanded from 2 to 27 sites in the DRC and from 1 to 56 decentralised sites in Burundi. RCCE activities reached 50 million people in 21 countries, with vaccine acceptance among high-risk groups rising from 44% to 87%. Only 938 000 doses (32%) of the 3.1 million vaccine doses delivered were administered. The evaluation revealed persistent structural challenges in last-mile vaccine delivery, contact tracing (due to stigma/funding) and weak regional collaborative research including fragmented regional research priorities.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The joint continental IMST is a new benchmark for response governance, successfully mobilising resources and scaling up diagnostics under unified co-leadership.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the need for sustained investment in national and sub-national health security architecture and highlight the importance of addressing structural challenges in vaccine delivery and regional research collaboration.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its descriptive nature and the lack of detailed statistical analysis. The evidence is moderate as it reflects operational achievements and challenges without deeper causal or quantitative analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the first year of the continental mpox response coordinated by the Joint Incident Management Support Team (IMST) in Africa. It highlights the epidemiological and operational outcomes, including 49,803 confirmed cases and 240 deaths, as well as the successful mobilisation of US$977 million in funding and expansion of laboratory testing capacity. However, it also identifies persistent challenges in vaccine delivery, contact tracing, and regional research collaboration. The study underscores the importance of a unified response framework and the need for sustained investment in health security. The findings suggest that while the IMST has set a new benchmark for response governance, further improvements are needed to address structural limitations and ensure equitable vaccine distribution.

title: Sentinel serosurvey for Mpox virus infection among key populations in India: Evidence of sporadic past exposure beyond travel-related cases

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to assess the prevalence of anti-Mpox virus IgG and IgM antibodies among key populations in India, addressing the need to understand the extent of past exposure to the virus beyond travel-related cases.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A multicentric, cross-sectional sentinel serosurvey was conducted between September 2023 to March 2024 across seven community-based organization sites in India, involving 1,790 participants aged 18-40 years.
analysis.methods: Serological testing using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) for anti-Mpox virus IgG and IgM antibodies was performed, with plaque reduction neutralisation test (PRNT50) used to assess functional neutralising antibodies against both MPXV and Vaccinia virus.
analysis.main_results: Among 1,790 participants, 14 (0.78%) tested positive for anti-Mpox virus IgG, with no IgM positivity detected. Geographic distribution ranged from 0.34% (Delhi NCR) to 2.07% (Kerala).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings establish very low Mpox virus seroprevalence (0.78%) among key populations in India, suggesting limited prior exposure. The absence of IgM antibodies indicates that infections were not recent and provides no evidence of ongoing community transmission during the study period.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings establish baseline sero-epidemiological evidence for Mpox in India and underscore the importance of periodic sentinel sero surveillance for early detection and outbreak preparedness.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the multicentric nature and potential sampling bias, as well as the absence of detailed information on the exact timing and context of past exposures. The evidence strength is moderate due to the limited sample size and the absence of recent infections.

analysis.summary_en: This study assessed the prevalence of anti-Mpox virus IgG and IgM antibodies among key populations in India, finding very low seroprevalence (0.78%) with no evidence of recent infections or ongoing community transmission.

title: Meta-analysis of Asymptomatic Monkeypox Virus Prevalence in Nonendemic Regions, 2022–2024

analysis.scope_and_question: This meta‐analysis examined the prevalence of asymptomatic monkeypox virus (MPXV) detection worldwide between 12 May 2022 and 13 Sept 2024, aiming to quantify how often MPXV is present without symptoms.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The authors searched the literature for relevant studies published during the specified period and applied a random‐effects model to synthesize prevalence estimates.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Across the included studies, the pooled prevalence of asymptomatic MPXV was 1.0 % (95 % prediction interval 0.1–11.2 %), with no significant variation by region or study design.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The analysis did not assess whether asymptomatic individuals could transmit MPXV, leaving a key uncertainty about the role of silent infections in ongoing transmission.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Further investigation into the viral dynamics that sustain MPXV circulation globally is warranted to inform control strategies.

analysis.summary_en: This meta‐analysis evaluated the prevalence of asymptomatic monkeypox virus (MPXV) detection worldwide from May 2022 to September 2024. By systematically searching the literature and applying a random‐effects model, the authors estimated a pooled prevalence of 1.0 % (95 % prediction interval 0.1–11.2 %). The prevalence did not differ significantly by geographic region or study design. However, the study did not examine the transmissibility of asymptomatic infections, leaving a critical gap in understanding silent transmission. The authors emphasize that MPXV continues to circulate globally and that the viral dynamics enabling its persistence remain poorly understood, underscoring the need for further research into MPXV’s ecological and epidemiological characteristics to guide effective public health interventions.

analysis.main_results: The study found that cidofovir-resistant poxviruses rapidly outcompete cidofovir-sensitive viruses when the two strains replicate in complete isolation, but when the two strains infect the same cell, the drug-resistant virus lost its competitive advantage over the sensitive strain.

title: Mpox Outbreak in Côte d'Ivoire during 2024: Epidemiological, Clinical, Virological and Outcome Features of Hospitalised Cases in Abidjan

analysis.research_question_and_background: To describe the epidemiological, clinical, virological and outcome features of Mpox patients hospitalised at the referral centre in Abidjan during the 2024 outbreak in Côte d'Ivoire, which totalled 89 confirmed cases nationwide. The study aimed to fill knowledge gaps regarding the local characteristics of the outbreak.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A descriptive observational study was conducted at the Department of Infectious and Tropical Diseases (SMIT), Treichville University Hospital, Abidjan, Côte d'Ivoire, from June to October 2024, involving 23 hospitalised patients with confirmed Mpox.
analysis.methods: Sociodemographic, clinical, virological (subclade typing by genomic sequencing), and outcome data were collected using a standardised questionnaire. Qualitative variables were described as counts and percentages, and quantitative variables as medians with interquartile range (IQR).
analysis.main_results: The study included 23 patients (median age: 20 years [IQR: 11–40]; 18 males, sex ratio: 3.6), with 100% skin rash, 95.7% fever, 91.3% headache, and 82.6% arthralgia. The main complication was bacterial superinfection (21.7%). The in-hospital case fatality rate was 4.3% (95% CI: 0.1–21.9).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The outbreak was both rural and urban, affected young unvaccinated patients, was dominated by subclade IIa, and had a generally favourable outcome. This is one of the first descriptions of the outbreak from Côte d'Ivoire.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest the need for strengthened surveillance, decentralised diagnosis, and access to vaccination. The study provides valuable insights into the local epidemiology and clinical features of the Mpox outbreak.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its small sample size and the fact that it is a descriptive observational study. The generalisability of the findings may be limited, and the exact 95% confidence interval for the in-hospital case fatality rate is wide.

analysis.summary_en: This study described the epidemiological, clinical, virological, and outcome features of 23 Mpox patients hospitalised in Abidjan, Côte d'Ivoire, during the 2024 outbreak. The outbreak was rural and urban, affected young unvaccinated patients, and was dominated by subclade IIa. The in-hospital case fatality rate was 4.3%, and the study highlights the need for strengthened surveillance and vaccination access.
